title: Jump Tables
concept: Jump tables make O(1) calls without branching by indexing an array of function pointers.

steps.title: Action function definitions
steps.explanation:
Prepare action functions with the same signature.

They must have the same signature to be stored in one pointer array.

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation: The main frame is created and prepares the jump table call flow.

steps.title: Optional variable declaration
steps.explanation:
`choice` represents the function index to call.

In practice, it is determined by user input/state value.

steps.title: Function pointer array (jump table)
steps.explanation:
Store function addresses in order in the `actions` array.

You can find the target function directly by index.
steps.keyInsight: The function name itself is the address of the function.

steps.title: range check
steps.explanation:
Verifies whether the index is within the range of the array.

If you call without checking, you risk accessing the wrong address.

steps.title: Calling a function with a jump table
steps.explanation:
Immediately calls the function selected with `actions[choice]();`.

Branching becomes possible without long if-elses.
steps.keyInsight: Select the executable function with one step of array indexing.

steps.title: Program exit
steps.explanation:
Exit with `return 0;`.

Bottom line: Jump tables are a fast and easy to scale branching pattern.

quiz.question: What is the biggest advantage of jump tables (function pointer arrays)?
options: Branch handling with O(1) time complexity
All functions can have the same name
quiz.explanation: Even if there are 100 cases, you can find the function to call with just one array indexing, which is much faster than if-else, which is a sequential comparison (O(N)).

misconceptions.wrong: A function pointer array can also contain functions of different types (parameters/return values).
misconceptions.correct:
no.
Since arrays can only contain the same type, the signatures of all functions must be the same.
misconceptions.why: It's the same as not being able to put floats in an int array.

keyTakeaway: Jump tables are a standard pattern for optimizing branching logic in state machines (FSMs) or instruction processors.
